claims.text: Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys exhibit rapid oxidation at 1100–1200°C.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys undergo oxide-scale spallation at 1100–1200°C in oxygen-rich environments.
Atomic layer deposition can produce an approximately 50 nm conformal Y2O3 coating on an RHEA surface.
An ALD-deposited Y2O3 coating will form a more adherent and protective oxide scale on an RHEA.
The Y2O3 coating will slow oxygen diffusion or ingress into the alloy.
A uniform Y2O3 surface layer will act as a reactive-element source.
The reactive-element source will facilitate formation of a continuous protective oxide scale.
The reactive-element source will improve adhesion and cohesiveness of the oxide scale.
The resulting protective scale will grow slowly and resist oxygen attack.
At 1150°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere for 100 hours, the coated alloy will have significantly lower oxidation mass gain than the untreated alloy.
Under the same exposure conditions, the coated alloy will show better oxide-scale adherence than the untreated alloy.
The untreated RHEA will have a mass gain greater than 120 mg/cm² after 100 hours under the specified conditions.
The untreated RHEA will undergo considerable oxide spallation under the specified conditions.
Coating defects or poor coating–alloy interfacial quality may diminish the protective effect.
Exposure substantially beyond 100 hours or exposure to additional corrosive species may diminish the protective effect.
Reactive-element additions have improved oxidation resistance in simpler alloy systems.
The quantitative oxidation improvement may vary with coating quality and alloy surface characteristics.
